pull_requests.body:
Aggregate acceptance counters cannot show whether DFlash lost a token because it missed the candidate set or chose the wrong candidate. This adds development-only completed-scratch capture to `decode-profile` and a model-free Python replay that separates those cases, checks conditional acceptance/calibration, and compares greedy, expected-prefix-length, Viterbi and scalar edge-score variants.

The accessor is defined only in the instrumented Runtime object. The capture uses the actual dispatch width to locate packed edge tables, omits position zero's unwritten predecessor rows, and records ordinary greedy cycles with every verify row. Replay reconstructs correct continuation from committed outputs, censors unavailable/terminal suffixes, and checks captured greedy choices and confidence before reporting.

Includes ten compressed real-model captures (552 lane cycles), exact prompt IDs, source/checkpoint identities, checksums, reproducible reports and a training/architecture analysis. The small correlated probes show selection headroom; look-ahead and scalar calibration have mixed results. **No trained checkpoint, production policy change or serving speedup is claimed.**

Related to #258 (selector capture/analysis portion) and #542. Stage attribution and stochastic-distribution capture remain separate work. Training and architecture experiments are tracked in #543–#548; the report also records the existing #499/#537 training PRs and the closed #259/#187 proposals.

Validation:

- 20 replay tests pass, including exhaustive DP references, FP32 ties, terminal censoring, complete batches, malformed captures and checksum/report reproduction for every archived capture.
- Full `make -j6 check` passes: CPU runtime, shader-validated Metal suites (including both MoE format sweeps), native builds, 1,335 Python tests with 27 skips, compileall, Ruff and architecture/source checks. Final replay additions pass all 20 tests separately; final CLI guards pass six invalid-input/context-limit checks.
- Final rebuilt tool captures/replays Qwen3.8-27B at B4 and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at B1; terminal-censoring and original dispatch-profiling smoke runs pass.
- Production Runtime preprocessing matches upstream main byte for byte; the new accessor is excluded from production. Original captures include a Metal shader-validated B3 run. CI results are reported independently on this PR.

[Analysis and recommendation coverage](https://github.com/linson007/splash/blob/feat/dflash-acceptance-diagnostics/dev/benchmarks/dflash-model-analysis.md) · [Measurements and reproduction](https://github.com/linson007/splash/blob/feat/dflash-acceptance-diagnostics/dev/benchmarks/results/dflash-acceptance-m5-pro/README.md)


<!-- dflash-real-cuda-smoke -->
### Trained-export native replay

[Published CUDA/native evidence](https://github.com/linson007/splash/blob/310e75d7f22e7a86f2141c5cf93e82aba62a9342/docs/experiments/qwen38-a100-smoke/README.md) adds native loading and capture/replay of the released Qwen3.8-27B draft and four actual CUDA-trained BF16 exports: **540 lane-cycles** on the same 4-bit target, INT8 KV, FP32 state, greedy decoding, all verification rows and frozen budget learning. All twenty sanitized published captures replay exactly. Non-draft input digests match across all five assemblies, and target output common prefixes agree in every comparison. No consistent acceptance improvement or throughput claim is supported by these four short prompts. This adds use of the existing diagnostics at `b4006b12cdd7`, without modifying its implementation.

The pinned teacher template defaults to thinking enabled with `xhigh` reasoning effort; native probes explicitly disabled thinking. This mode mismatch, together with the BF16/low-bit target difference and short captures, prevents a matched-distribution effectiveness conclusion. Future capture controls should make thinking mode explicit and include it in cache/run provenance.

pull_requests.body:
Measures proposal-policy alternatives against the same full target distribution and correct predecessor context. The reference compares existing, history-only and history-plus-prefix penalties on fixed candidate support, reporting overlap, target tail mass and proposal entropy. Prompt occurrences activate repetition; presence/frequency count generated output.

Related to #545. This implements the numerical measurement/reference stage; the research issue stays open for deployed distribution capture and serving qualification.

Validation:

- Full repository Python suite passed: **1325 tests, 27 expected skips**, after building the required native binary in this worktree.
- Seven focused tests passed: target-tail preservation, signed penalties, default controls, within-block counts, greedy tie order, sampled frequencies, context mismatch rejection, and CLI/schema round-trip.
- The exact accept-plus-residual reference reproduces arbitrary full target distributions on 100 small cases, including disjoint proposal support and target tail tokens.
- Ruff lint/format and architecture boundaries passed; production native build succeeded locally.

```sh
python -m unittest dev.tests.tools.test_dflash_policy_overlap -v
python -m dev.benchmarks.dflash_policy_overlap capture.json --output report.json
```

Inputs must supply the **actual full target p after request filtering** and correctly bound proposal scores. The existing greedy capture in #550 does not contain that distribution. Fixture provenance is explicit and is not real-model improvement evidence. Target top-k/top-p/min-p, stops, thinking and constraints are already reflected in p; this tool changes no runtime policy, retrieval support, proposal q buffer or rejection correction. The CPU reference is not FP32/Metal numerical parity. Native sampled capture, mixed-lane/state tests and paired latency/acceptance measurements remain open.

pull_requests.body:
Adds a native fresh-versus-restored-prefix probe and a matched-context comparator for #548. The probe explicitly materializes a page-aligned prefix, snapshots the real composite state, moves the request to another state lane, restores it, rebuilds draft rings and resumes the same prompt. Fresh controls use identical materialization and prefill chunk boundaries.

Captured context hashes include the pending anchor. The comparator rejects mismatched model/prompt/precision/policy/budget settings, pairs only identical contexts and reports censored acceptance, proposal changes, verify-row choices, selector-confidence changes and optional BF16 final-hidden drift. Adaptive capture can freeze the prior/cost seed, avoiding online timing-learning confounds. Native scratch matches beyond retained/verified rows are censored.

### Native evidence

The checked-in, hash-verified archive contains 12 captures / 48 cycles / 24 matched-context pairs on Apple M5 Pro (48 GiB, macOS 26.6): released dense and MoE DFlash2 drafts with their MLX 4-bit targets, 2112/8256-token source-review prompts, INT8/BF16 KV, and full/frozen-adaptive verify budgets.

- Proposals and retained lengths were unchanged in all 24 matched pairs.
- Final-hidden relative L2 maxima were 0.044–0.057 per case. Selector confidence moved even with unchanged proposals.
- In one frozen-budget MoE cycle, fresh/restored chose six/five verify rows and both retained three tokens. This motivates calibration/cost measurement after restore; it is not evidence of lost acceptance or a speedup.
- The treatment includes snapshot restore **and** lane movement. These data do not isolate context-window quantization from every numerical effect.

### Validation

- 26 capture/replay/comparison tests passed, including all archived file hashes and exact report reproduction, BF16 numerical drift, context mismatch rejection and adaptive-budget censoring.
- B3/two-cycle capture passed with `MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1`, including hidden-row readback.
- Nine native CLI error guards passed; the instrumented native benchmark and production library rebuilt successfully.
- Production `Runtime.cpp` preprocesses byte-identically to upstream main (SHA256 `11c4aac9285dae98a7f4db0f053072bfe83ac57beb99d77b3ed31c1130a77f38`); extra accessors/reset hooks exist only in instrumented builds.
- Ruff lint/format, architecture boundaries and diff whitespace checks passed.

Additional test limitation: combined `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1` hit a `prefill_gdn_scan_vh32` threadgroup-memory assertion (35072 > 32768) on this host. That extra check did **not** pass; it occurs in the unchanged target kernel, and the **same assertion reproduced on the unchanged #550 baseline binary**. Shader-validation-only capture passed. The failure is recorded in the validation artifact.

### Dependencies and remaining gates

Ready-for-review follow-up to #550; merge #550 first. Based on `ef0e95d4fa09f265f1cb071d43591ff32367b372`; upstream `main` remains the base, so #550's parent capture changes are visible until it merges. Review only this follow-up here: [experiment diff](https://github.com/linson007/splash/compare/ef0e95d4fa09f265f1cb071d43591ff32367b372...b4006b12cdd7e0eff0b759b2f5f1aa9d53e93610).

The research issue stays open. These are short source-review mechanics probes, not a broad long-context retrieval or task-quality benchmark. SSD/suspend restoration, larger contexts, direct ring reconstruction references, paired serving timings and any trained global-memory/window experiment remain unqualified. Capture I/O is unsuitable for throughput claims. No production architecture or checkpoint default is changed.

Closes #3284. This repo's rules ask a feature's scope to be agreed in an issue first; there has been no comment there, so treat this as that proposal — the feature is opt-in, measured, and the whole record is in `docs/BATCHING.md`. Happy to discuss scope before merge.

## Problem

On a Mac the engine answers one request at a time and every other client queues (`docs/MAC.md`: "--parallel (batch slots) is not ported"). One person plus their coding agents — a small office — leave the machine between requests at ~2 GB/s of weight reads when the bandwidth is several times that, while the same model on a PC gains multiples by decoding waiting requests together.

## Result

`--batch N` on the Metal engine runs N conversations in one window. Measured on an M1 Max (64 GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS), 21–23 Oct 2026:

| Run | Aggregate | Same prompts alone | Replies vs solo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 slots, greedy, 128 tok | 37.5 tok/s | 23 / 25 tok/s | both byte-identical |
| 2 slots, sampled (temp 0.7, seed 7), 64 tok | 42.7 tok/s | 23 / 25 tok/s | both byte-identical |
| 4 slots, greedy, 128 tok | 34.7 tok/s | 23–32 tok/s | 2 of 4 byte-identical; the other 2 answered their own question fluently and chose a different word at one near tie (tokens 88 and 13) |

The interleave cases hold too: a 4888-token prompt reads in while slots decode (126 slot tokens during the read); a read that gives way at a chunk boundary (`YIELDED 2 1024`) goes on in its slot; a request stopped part-way in a slot hands back to the solo path and reproduces its solo reply; a next turn reads from its slot's parked state; a prompt chunk cancelled mid-read resumes from its checkpoint (`1024 reused + 3866 read`). With `STRATA_BATCH_VERIFY=1` the engine byte-compares each slot region's GDN states, QSA cells, tails, dead and pooled rows and PLE history against the window that made them, and reported all match for every region; the per-step kernel captures show each row's folds up to the batched PLE block bit-exact against its solo run.

The default path is unchanged: without `--batch` the window builds and runs exactly the commands it did before, and every unit gate passes both ways.

## Approach

- The arena carves a region per slot — each reply's full state in the solo window's own layout (about 3.8 GB with these settings, so the batch count is a memory choice, not a speed choice; the engine prints the cost at start, and refuses with a clear line when the regions do not fit). Parking already kept this state per conversation, so `--batch` combines with `--conversation-cache-mib`: a prompt reads through the main window and is copied into its slot's region before its rows first run.
- The batch window builds the solo one-token dispatch list once per row. Every kernel that touches state takes the row index and reads and writes only its own region, and every GEMV keeps the plain tile — no CUDA grouped tiles, no doorbell kernels, no graph capture. What a window saves per step is the fixed cost the rows share: the device-flag cut handshake (each segment gated by a ~90 us flag spin, not an event pair), the sampler round trip, the launch gaps.
- One binding fix the captures found, worth naming: a batch row's GDN step binds the prepared activation at its own slice, and the per-16 sums it writes for the quantized-input GEMVs landed at that bound base — rows after the first wrote sums nobody read and past the buffer, into the arena's next allocation. The sums have their own binding now; the solo window and the first row address them bit-identically to before, and `gdn_parity`'s new plane-row check pins it (it fails with the pre-fix address and passes after).
- Where a batched row can differ from solo is measured, not guessed: a 315-probe per-step trajectory for every row shows the first difference is the fold leaving the batched PLE block — a few kernels batch the rows in one dispatch and round differently than the per-token solo sequence, at fractions of a percent, amplified by fold cancellations. (Which kernel exactly rounds differently is unconfirmed static analysis.)

## Validation

Revisions and environment. The measurements were made on this fork's Mac line at `783a55fc` (the batch commits `2d50ea42..783a55fc`), M1 Max, 64 GB, macOS 27, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS. `upstream/main` was merged into the branch after the runs (merge commit `1ff3a385`, main at `5c8dd322`); the post-merge tree rebuilds on this machine, and the merge touches none of the batch code.

**Passed:**

- `metal/tests` host gates on `783a55fc` (M1 Max, macOS 27): `gdn_parity` (incl. the new plane-row check and its negative control), `gdn_prompt_parity`, `window_cells_test`, `host_sampler_parity`, `runtime_hello`, `moe_mm_parity`, `gemv_parity`, `qsa_parity`, `buffer_free_test` — all green.
- `tools/batch_interleave_test.py` run twice — prompt reads interleaving with slot decoding, the yield at a chunk boundary, the stop-into-slot hand-back, the parked-state next turn, the mid-read checkpoint resume.
- `STRATA_BATCH_VERIFY=1` on the 2- and 4-slot runs — per-slot state byte-compare all match, per-step 315-probe trajectories printed for every row.
- `tools/token_chain.py` / `tools/prompt_chain.py` on the 47 GB shard (30.5 tok/s, 147 tok/s; the 2-chunk wrap past `maxBufferLength`).
- Solo rates with `--batch` absent match this branch's pre-batch measurements (23–33 tok/s) — the solo path did not regress.

**Failed:**

- The harnesses' byte-identity gate — 2 of 4 slots at `--batch 4`, and three interleave slots across two runs. At every miss both continuations answer their own prompt and the window's logits differ from solo's by the PLE-block noise above, so argmax breaks the tie the other way (the interleave runs print both texts: a colon against a comma, one period, `static int` against `int`). `docs/BATCHING.md`'s Metal section carries the same doctrine CUDA already ships: token identity of a batched row is luck, coherence and no cross-talk are the contract. With serialized admissions the flips repeat exactly (4 slots: 88 and 13 across independent runs); when prompt reads interleave with decoding, arrival timing changes what each row shares its dispatches with and which slot flips can move between runs.

**Not run:**

- The CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds (this is a macOS host without an NVIDIA or AMD card). The shared `src/core` and `src/program` hunks sit inside `#if defined(STRATA_GPU_METAL)` and the non-Metal bodies are unchanged text, but I cannot certify a build I did not run — CI must.
- Other Apple Silicon shapes (only this M1 Max: no M3/M4/M5, no Studio or Ultra), `--batch-groups` pipelining on Metal, layer split with batch, batch counts past 4 (the regions would not fit 64 GB with the model), multi-day serving under real user load, and vision towers with batch.

## What is in this branch, honestly

The seven batch commits (`2d50ea42..783a55fc`) sit on this fork's Mac line, which upstream has not taken: conversation parking on macOS, the device-flag cut handshake, M1/M2 GEMV speedups, the purge/hash fix, and merges of the still-open #3301, #3527, #3615 and #3333 plus my open #3287 and #2645. That is why the commit list is longer than the feature; `upstream/main` is merged into the branch (`1ff3a385`), so the diff applies cleanly, and the batch changes are marked in the commit subjects. I am happy to rebase onto whichever pieces land first, or to split.

## Limits

Opt-in and experimental on Macs. No layer split or pipelined groups in a batch window. Each extra slot costs a full per-conversation region in RAM (15.4 GB for four here). The gain is real on this box (up to ~1.7x at two slots) and falls as rows grow; nobody has measured more than four.

## How to try it

```
tools/metal_batch_try.sh 2 2 128
```

It starts the engine with `--batch`, runs the same prompts alone and together, byte-compares every reply, and refuses to run while another big server holds the memory (see the script's header). For sampled rows add `--keys "temperature=0.7 seed=7"`.

pull_requests.body:
## Problem and result

The Mac engine served one request at a time: `--batch` (the config's `"parallel"`) was not ported, so a second client waited for the first client's whole answer. With two coding-agent sessions on one Mac, a long reply in one left the other stuck until it ended.

After this change `"parallel": N` (or `strata launch --parallel N`) runs on the Metal engine. Metal has no co-decode, so the slots time-share the one decode window and the gain is concurrency, not throughput: a request that arrives while another is answering gets its first token after the next batch window instead of after the other's whole answer, and each slot decodes exactly what it would alone. Off unless `parallel` is set (as on a PC); a Mac that does not set it runs the same code as before (every branch is under `STRATA_GPU_METAL` and `o.batch > 0`).

## Related discussion

None. Opened directly, as a draft: see "Not run". Independent of #3756 (both touch `window.cpp` and `MAC.md` at different places and merge in either order).

## Approach

- `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`: a `SlotStore` per slot holds a copy of the window's persistent state (the GDN recurrences and conv histories, the PLE history, each QSA layer's K/V, scales, indexer tail and pooled keys) plus `hp_` and the n-gram window. `slot_step` brings a slot's state into the live buffers if it is not there, runs the window's own `run(1 token) + commit(1)`, and marks it dirty; the state is written back only when something else takes the window (`leave_slot()` at the solo `window_run`, `window_reset`, `window_checkpoint_restore` and the prompt read), so consecutive steps of one slot copy nothing. The positional buffers are copied up to the conversation's extent plus a margin (cells past it are rewritten before they are read, as `commit()` already relies on). `slot_capture` runs a pending lazy fold first (a solo spec window's), so a stored state never depends on the scratch inputs. The dispatch cache is untouched: it binds the live buffers by their stable handles; only the bytes behind them change. `batch_fit()` once the window is up: as many slots as fit in what `cudaMemGetInfo` reports free with 1 GiB kept, else batching off, said in the log. `STRATA_METAL_BATCH_TRACE=1` prints admissions, restores and steps.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`, under `STRATA_GPU_METAL`: the slot allocation keeps empty `SessionState` placeholders (the window owns the slots), the slot-session `init_slots` loop is skipped, `copy_to_slot` is the window's admission (the live state the solo path just read), `copy_from_slot` restores the slot's state and, with a turn checkpoint, that checkpoint's running state (`conversation_checkpoint_restore`, as the CUDA path), and the batch window steps the active slots one after the other instead of `run_slot_rows` + `commit_slots`. `batch_mtp` is off on Metal (one token per slot per window; the solo path keeps its drafts, so a request alone is not put in a slot, as on a PC).
- Docs: `MAC.md` (the limit replaced by what it does and costs; the trace line), `BATCHING.md` (the Mac notes).

Compatibility: no new flag, config key or protocol line; the CUDA and HIP code is unchanged. Sampling in slots: the Mac engine decodes greedily on every path (`sample_tokens` is a stub on Metal), so slots do too; `set_slot_sampling` is a no-op there, as before.

## Validation

Environment: MacBook Pro M1 Max, 64 GB, macOS 26.5.2; Apple clang 21.0.0, metal-cpp_26, llama.cpp 3cf0325; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO Q2_0 with `--spec 2 --mtp`, 32K context, `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0`. Revision d1aeb50c, `ninja -C build-metal strata` after `cmake -S metal -B build-metal -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DMETAL_CPP_DIR=... -DSTRATA_GGML_DIR=...`. The two scripts are the ones `BATCHING.md` names for the PC engines, unchanged.

**Passed:**

- `python3 tools/batch_test.py --exe build-metal/strata --config strata-q2_0.json --batch 2 --n 2 --max-new 64 --mt-min "" --extra "--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000"` -> `slot 0: 64 tokens, solo 64: IDENTICAL`, `slot 1: 64 tokens, solo 64: IDENTICAL`; `batch: 2 slots, 128 tokens; admissions 1.3s; then 6.8s -> aggregate 15.8 tok/s overall, 17.1 tok/s from the first batch token` (the solo runs decoded 64 tokens in 2.8-3.0 s with drafts).
- `python3 tools/batch_interleave_test.py --exe build-metal/strata --config strata-q2_0.json --max-new 100 --long 2000 --yield skip --extra "--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000 --no-prefill-borrow"` -> exit 0; every comparison IDENTICAL: the three slots (A, B, the 1,983-token C) against solo; A's next turn from its slot; E admitted beside D's read; D read whole; A back on the solo path after 52 slot tokens; F (A's history without the reply's thinking) continued from the slot's turn checkpoint; 7b (F2 after 8 unrelated GENs, from the slot). `--yield skip` because a Mac reads a prompt in one piece (below).
- The engine's fit line at start: `--batch 3: 3 slots, each a 0.55 GiB copy of the window's state (42.87 GiB free)`
- Two HTTP clients on `serve.server` with `"parallel": 2`: a request sent 4 s into another's 220-token answer got its first token after 1.1 s and finished in 1.5 s while the first kept decoding (218 tokens in 11.1 s); each answer equal to the same prompt alone.

**Failed:**

- None observed on the submitted revision. (An earlier revision failed the interleave test's turn-checkpoint steps, F and 7b: `copy_from_slot` ignored the checkpoint and continued from the slot's end state. Fixed: the checkpoint's running state is restored.)

**Not run:**

- CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds of `src/program/generate.cpp`: the changes there are `#if defined(STRATA_GPU_METAL)` branches and one `#if !defined` around the existing slot-session init, but I have no PC to build on. That is why this is a draft; a build on one of them would settle it.
- `--yield` (`BYIELD`, a prompt read giving way at a chunk boundary): the Metal prompt path reads a prompt in one call, so it cannot give way; the interleave test ran with `--yield skip`.
- Pictures in slots, `--batch-mtp` (off on Metal), more than 2 slots (3 were used by the interleave test; 8 were not), a context above 32K with slots.

## Limits

- Concurrency, not throughput: the weights are read from the mapped model every step either way. Measured here, two slots together decoded at 15.8-17.1 tok/s against a solo request's ~22 tok/s with drafts (a slot has none).
- A slot's state copy costs memory by the context: about 0.55 GiB at 32K, 1 GiB at 64K, 1.9 GiB at 128K, 3.6 GiB at 256K (the K/V and pooled keys are copied up to the conversation's extent, the GDN state in full, ~120 MB). At 256K on a 64 GB Mac not two slots fit; the engine says so and runs one at a time.
- Switching between slots costs the GDN copy twice (~120 MB each way) plus the conversation's K/V; per-slot GDN buffers bound by handle would remove it (the dispatch cache would then need a key per slot). Not done here.
- A prompt is read in one piece, so slots pause for the read (no `BYIELD`).

pull_requests.body:
## Problem and result

On a layer split of four stages, `--pipeline-windows 2` keeps two speculation windows in flight. On four GP100 dies (two PH402 boards, compute capability 6.0) a window that starts from a verdict takes about 38 ms and a speculated window about 19 ms, and each stage spends much of a window waiting for the one ahead of it. The pipelined loop's draft chain also stops at 7 outputs, which caps what a third window could verify. Deeper speculation inside one window does not pay on this card (every extra verify row costs about 2.2-2.5 ms per stage in my measurements); a third window in flight adds no rows to any window. Today `--pipeline-windows` is clamped to 2, so `3` is accepted and ignored.

With `--pipeline-windows 3` on three or more stages, three windows are in flight: the last stage verifies the oldest window while the earlier stages run two speculated ones, and a misprediction is undone stage by stage as soon as each stage is free of its doomed window. **Measured on four GP100 dies with every expert resident in VRAM (no CPU or PCIe share)**, decode goes 54.22 -> 56.12 tok/s (+3.5%; two runs per arm in the order 2, 3, 3, 2; eight decode prompts, token-weighted), with every reply identical. The gain needs a fast drafter: with the generic draft kernels it was +0.15%; with the Pascal Q8_0 draft head of #3751 it is +3.5% (details below). Without `--pipeline-windows 3` the engine runs today's pw-2 loop with the same allocations, captures and log lines.

## Related discussion

none; the drafter it pays with is #3751

## Approach

Seven commits, in order; each builds.

- `mtp`: the draft chain grows to up to 11 outputs, step by step (`MtpDrafter::kChainMax`, graphs for steps 1..11), with a source-copy event the new loop waits on, and `chain_cap()` (the outputs a chain may queue). Only a caller of `set_chain_max` above 7 gets the longer chain, so the output clamp at the context end is unchanged for everyone else. A parity program (`mtp_chain_parity`, configured only when `STRATA_MTP_PARITY_BASE` names the commit before this one) checks the chain against the code it replaces.
- `pl_sched` (new `src/program/pl_sched.{hpp,cpp}`): the pipelined decode loop as a host-side state machine. It decides which window launches, waits, commits, is undone or is re-staged, and emits operations; it calls no GPU code. `pl_sched_test` (CPU only, `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`, built with `--target pl_sched_test`) runs it against a symbolic GPU: a recorded decode trace, random worlds, every small world with every ending, and today's pw-2 loop transcribed operation for operation.
- `generate.cpp`, the engine side: a slot pool of depth + 1 slots per stage (a verifier, a hand-off per boundary, a GDN snapshot per front stage), taken from a free list instead of `seq % 2`, so a new window never writes a hand-off that a doomed window is still reading; the extra room is kept out of the expert caches at start-up. `PlIoFns` turns each scheduler operation into the verifier / snapshot / drafter call it names. The new loop is a separate branch before today's pw-2 loop, which is not changed; it emits a verdict as the pw-2 loop does, including #879 (non-finite logits end the request), the PCIe auto step after each verdict, and the adaptive thread pinned to the aux CPUs and named.
- Modes: `--pipeline-windows 3` runs depth 3 (4 slots); `STRATA_PIPELINE_UNDO_PER_STAGE=1` runs depth 2 with the per-stage undo (3 slots); `STRATA_PIPELINE_SLOTS=k` sizes the pool. `STRATA_MTP_CHAIN_MAX` (7..11, default 11) and `STRATA_MTP_CHAIN_STOP` (default 1) tune depth 3's chain. Test hooks (the switch file's new keys, `STRATA_PIPELINE_CHECK_STATE`, forced misses) need `STRATA_PIPELINE_DEBUG=1`.
- Fallbacks to today's loop, each said once: fewer than three stages (`--pipeline-windows 3` is then 2), a pool that does not fit at start-up or whose captures fail (it shrinks back to two slots), the draft layer on the first stage, a first window merged with the prompt's tail, a scheduler configuration that fails `Sched::check`, and a chain that could not be captured at 11 outputs (it stays at 7).
- Bit-identical by construction: only the oldest window reaches the last stage and only its output is emitted; a mispredicted window is undone on every stage before its replacement reaches that stage; the per-stage undo changes when a stage acts, never the order of operations in a stage's stream.
- Default path: with `--pipeline-windows` 0..2 and none of the new switches the pool is two slots and every request runs the pw-2 loop, with the same reservations and captures. One change reaches it: the drafter's staging rows grow from 2T to max(2T, T + 11) (19 instead of 16 rows at T = 8), so later buffers in its arena move, its mapped output arrays hold 16 entries instead of T, and it keeps 12 step events instead of 8. The bytes read and written and the operations are the same (checked end to end below).
- Builds: `pl_sched.cpp` is added to the `strata` target in the main CMake (CUDA/HIP) and in `metal/CMakeLists.txt`. The scheduler is host code with no backend-specific parts; SYCL has its own `generate.cpp` and is not touched. `verify.cpp` is not touched.

Independent of #3455 and #3751: this branch is main plus these commits and needs neither to build or to be correct; #3751 is what makes depth 3 pay on GP100.

## Validation

**Environment note: everything below was measured with every expert resident in VRAM on four GP100 dies** (two PH402 SKU 200 boards, 32 GB HBM2 per die, 128 GB in all; the Swift 1.5 IQ3_S pack fits whole: no CPU share, no PCIe share, no adaptive tier). A single card, three stages, or experts in RAM were not measured. HIP, SYCL and Metal were not built.

**Measured revision.** The GPU numbers come from main e88ee39d (engine 0.1.45.3) plus a stack of my opt-in GP100 changes that includes these seven commits. This branch is the same seven commits rebased onto main 011c9e60 (engine 0.1.47): one conflict (the `strata` target's new HIP delay-load block in `CMakeLists.txt`; both kept), and the one change upstream made to the pw-2 loop in between (the adaptive thread's name) mirrored in the new loop. It builds (below), but I have not re-measured it on the GPUs.

Rig: four GP100 dies (application clocks 715 MHz memory / 1050 MHz graphics, 140 W cap), Windows 11, driver 581.80 (TCC), CUDA 12.9, VS 2022. Build: `-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=60`, ggml at the pinned 3cf03257f, unpatched. Model: Swift 1.5 IQ3_S (abliterated GSQ-RCO GGUF, dense matrices in Q8_0) with an MTP drafter. Engine arguments, the same on every arm except `--pipeline-windows`: `--serve --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.85 --mtp <drafter> --max-context 1048576 --kv int8 --layer-split 12,24,36 --mtp-window 8192 --pipeline-windows 2|3 --conversation-cache-mib 32768 --conversation-cache-slots 8 --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4`. Environment, the same on every arm: `STRATA_Q8_SM60=1 STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1 STRATA_PREFILL_PIPE=70 STRATA_MMQ_RESIDENT_SORT_NE=1 STRATA_DF_BRANCH=1 STRATA_FUSE_DECODE=1 STRATA_FUSE_WAIT=2 STRATA_SIDE_MIXER=2 STRATA_GR_UP75=1 STRATA_B6_MMVQ_ROWS=1 STRATA_ADAPT_LAG=2 STRATA_ADAPT_NOWAIT=1 STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`, plus the stack's `STRATA_EXPERT_NIBBLE=1` (#3455's 4-bit slots), `STRATA_SPLIT_COMMIT_ASYNC=1` (an async split commit, not posted) and `STRATA_MTP_Q8_SM60=1` (#3751).

**Passed:**
- Speed, pw 2 against pw 3, one fresh engine per run, runs in the order 2, 3, 3, 2, greedy. Eight decode requests per run: five short prompts (400-512 tokens out), an 8K-token read + 300 out, a fresh 26K-token read + 400 out, an 88K-token conversation + 400 out.
  - Decode, tokens out / decode time, token-weighted: pw 2 54.22 and 54.22, pw 3 56.08 and 56.15 tok/s: **+3.5%**. Per request, pw 2 -> pw 3: +3.4, +1.5, +4.4, +3.6, +4.6% (the short prompts), +4.9% (8K), +2.6% (26K), +3.1% (88K).
  - Per window (from `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING`): a speculated window 19.02 -> 16.58 ms; a window that starts from a verdict 38.81 -> 37.85 ms; at pw 3, windows held behind one hit 15.19 ms, behind two 17.86 ms.
  - Every reply hash the same in all four runs. Every pw 3 request logged `depth3 ... mode B slots 4`; no fallback line in any run.
- The same comparison without #3751 (generic draft kernels; one run per arm, part of a longer ladder of runs): +0.15% (51.73 -> 51.81 tok/s). There the held windows took 19.29 / 20.82 ms instead of 15.19 / 17.86: the chain runs on the last die beside the last stage's verify and reads the 276 MiB draft head every step, which eats what the third window saves. The window counts and the number of windows held behind two hits were within 1% of the runs with #3751.
- Parity, pw 2 against pw 3 (same stack, one run each): 15 requests, including prompt reads up to 250K tokens and a parked-and-continued conversation. Every reply hash and every main-model `STRATA_STATE_HASH` item (GDN, PLE, tail, pooled, KV) equal. Two kinds of difference, both in state that is never read: the drafter's own K/V hash (`mtp=`) differs on the six requests with prompts of 26K tokens or more (all shorter ones equal), and the hash of the KV cells past the committed end (`stale`) on three. The `mtp=` hash also covers ring cells outside the drafter's window, which it never reads and a new conversation does not clear, and the deeper chain leaves different leftovers there. That is my explanation from the code, not proven cell by cell: on two of the six the last 24 cells differ too, which it does not cover.
- Default path: the stack's engine with none of its switches set (pw 2) against main e88ee39d unchanged, the same 15 requests: every reply hash and every `STRATA_STATE_HASH` item equal, `mtp=` included.
- Memory: peak VRAM +280 MiB on each front-stage die and +224 MiB on the last die at pw 3.
- Earlier, on my older tree (0.1.41 base, the same design): the new loop in depth-2 mode against today's loop -0.02%, the verdict sequence 10 of 10 identical; the per-stage undo alone +1.8%; depth 3 +3.4%; 11 of 11 replies identical, including a reply that ends at EOS, parking a conversation and continuing it.
- `pl_sched_test` on this branch (sm_60 build, Windows, CPU only, 368 s): `PASS (0 failures)`. The recorded trace (6 requests, 1,280 verdicts), random worlds (about 1,000,000 verdicts per mode) and every small world with every ending (1,119,744 runs per mode), each in modes N2 (today's loop), B0 and B, all with 0 failures; today's pw-2 loop against the scheduler's depth-2 mode: 802,830 worlds, every one the same line for line.
- Builds of this branch at 93b00c28: sm_60 with `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON` (`strata pl_sched_test`) and sm_86 without it (`strata`), both clean. No warnings in `pl_sched*` (built with `strata_warnings`); on the lines this branch adds to `generate.cpp`, only `getenv` C4996, as elsewhere in the file.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** HIP, SYCL and Metal builds (no such machine here; the HIP and Metal `strata` targets now compile `pl_sched.cpp`, which neither of my builds checks on those toolchains). A GPU run of this exact branch on main 011c9e60 (the numbers above are from e88ee39d + the stack). Faster cards and three-stage splits (only four stages measured). `mtp_chain_parity` on this branch (it was run on my older tree). Gcc / clang builds of `pl_sched_test`. `--batch`. The draft layer on the first stage and a first window merged with the prompt's tail (both fall back to today's loop, not exercised). Packs other than Swift 1.5 IQ3_S.

## Limits

- Three or more stages only; with two, `--pipeline-windows 3` is 2.
- The gain depends on the drafter's cost per step and on the acceptance rate: on GP100 it needs #3751's draft head (+0.15% without it). I have no number for faster cards, where windows are shorter.
- Windows held behind two hits take about 2.7 ms longer than those held behind one (17.86 against 15.19 ms), more than an event model of the loop predicted; that is the open tuning item.
- +224-280 MiB of VRAM per die for the two extra slots.
- About 1,000 lines in `generate.cpp`, 1,100 in the scheduler and 3,400 in its test.
